A small wooden raft floats near the center, carrying a flask and three little cups; one cup sits a careful handspan apart from the others.
Five yuzu fruits bob on the surface, three nudged together against the far rim, their dimpled skin catching the faint glow from the lantern.
A folded white cloth rests balanced on the stone rim, its four corners pressed into near-perfect alignment except one, which lifts in a slow curl.
A cotton robe hangs from a single wooden peg under the eave, its sash looped twice over the same peg and knotted rather than tied in a bow.
A pair of wooden clogs sits on a flat stone at the step; the left clog angles outward just enough to suggest a hurried step and a quick return.
A bamboo pipe pours a thin, steady stream into the pool; the rock beneath it has been worn smooth into a shallow dish from years of the same falling thread of water.
A stone lantern stands at the pool's edge, a real flame small and upright inside its window, casting a faint gold patch across the nearest rim stone.
A wooden bucket floats low and heavy in the water, a bamboo scoop hooked over its lip with the handle resting at a slight lean.
A basket of seven glass bottles sits sunk in the cold side channel, six standing upright and one leaning out at an angle, its neck above the water.

A narrow wooden shelf pegged flush to the rim holds a round cup painted with a single pine sprig and a folded fan, its paper face plain cream with one small painted leaf, ribs pressing open the faintest gap.
A long-handled dipper rests across three rim stones, its bowl tipped just past center so one more nudge would send it sliding.
A low three-legged stool sits on the wet stone, two legs flush and one leg trimmed shorter, a thin sliver of cedar wedged beneath it to steady it.
A stack of five folded towels sits under a small roofed shelf, the topmost towel unfolded and spread, its near corner draped over the shelf edge.
A small iron brazier glows on a dry flat stone, a round kettle sitting on it with its lid cocked to one side, letting a slow curl of vapor escape.
A lidded lacquered box sits on a dry stone, its surface painted with a single waning moon on a plain ground, the lid settled but not pressed fully shut.
A tray of black and white pebbles sits on a flat rock mid-game, one white stone placed apart from the cluster as though the next move was interrupted.
A tangerine rests on a rim stone, peeled halfway, its curled skin folded back and laid beside it in three connected sections still holding their shape.
A paper lantern leans against a mossy boulder where someone set it down in haste, its wire bail hooked on a small stone nub to keep it from rolling.
A bundle of cut cedar branches steeps in the pool, tied with a length of cord whose loose end floats free and drifts in a slow circle.
A woven straw mat has been rolled tight and stood upright against the wooden fence post, a thin strip of cord wound around it once and tucked rather than tied.
A hand-broom and a round pail rest beside the stepping stones, the broom leaned against the pail's handle so neither can tip without taking the other along.
A small ceramic cup sits on the rim, its body bearing a fine gold seam that follows the entire curve of a crack repaired with careful lacquer and gold dust.
A bamboo rail runs along the poolside, a towel slung over it near one end, that end trailing down to rest on the stone below in a loose fold.
A wooden ladle stands wedged upright between two rim stones, its handle pressed into the gap at an angle that will not let it drift or tip.
A small hollowed gourd floats near the rim, a thin cord tied through a hole at its neck and looped around a knob of stone so it cannot wander.
